recipes.name: Indian Chicken Curry (Murgh Kari)
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breast halves

steps.text: Sprinkle the chicken breasts with 2 teaspoons salt. Heat 1 to 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over high heat. Brown chicken in batches, adding more oil as needed, until partially cooked and golden on all sides. Transfer browned chicken breasts to a plate and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium and add onion, garlic, and ginger to the oil remaining in the skillet. Cook and stir until onion turns soft and translucent, 5 to 8 minutes. Stir curry powder, cumin, turmeric, coriander, cayenne, and 1 tablespoon of water into the onion mixture; allow to heat together for about 1 minute while stirring.
Add tomatoes, yogurt, 1 tablespoon chopped cilantro, and 1 teaspoon salt to the mixture; stir to combine.

Return chicken breast to the skillet along with any juices on the plate. Pour in 1/2 cup water and bring to a boil, turning the chicken to coat with the sauce. Sprinkle garam masala and 1 tablespoon cilantro over the chicken.

Cover the skillet and simmer until chicken breasts are no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, about 20 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).
Drizzle with lemon juice to serve. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Indian Chicken Curry (Murgh Kari)
raw_recipe.description: This Indian chicken curry simmers chicken breasts in a homemade curry sauce made with yogurt, tomatoes, fresh ginger, garam masala, and warm spices.

video.description: The recipe in this video is a really good method to prepare spicy Indian chicken curry. It's pretty easy to make and tastes really good! Serve this dish over basmati rice for an easy meal.

review.reviewBody: If I'm going to review a recipe it will only be if I stayed true to the instructions. I can't justify giving a bad review after writing about all the changes I made. Well guess what? This recipe is freakin great! Every bite was like a party in my mouth. Young and old, everyone enjoyed it. The leftovers were even better the next day. DON'T CHANGE A THING.

I'm sorry but I have followed the exact recipe above and this curry is completely inedible. As mentioned by others - the yoghurt has curdled after being brought to a boil. I have made many curries (using authentic recipe books) and never has this ever happened. Most often the yoghurt is added at the end and only stirred in and heated for a short period of time. It's watery, curdled, inedible and quite frankly disgusting. It's going straight in the bin - what a waste of chicken!

This is one of our family favorites. We have dietary restrictions so have made some adaptations. We substitute coconut milk for the yogurt and it tastes awesome. We also cut the the spice down a tad bit for our taste and use our home bottled tomatoes which makes it extra yummy. Great recipe. Another side tip: It takes a little extra time due to measuring all the dry ingredients. We use this recipe so much that we now get four little containers and measure out the ingredients for four separate batches, that way, when we cook it the next time we just open our little container with the premeasured ingredients and making it is so much faster.

Tasty dish! Cooked as per the instructions but substituted dairy yogurt for coconut yogurt. Rested the breasts after cooking and sliced them up - super tender. Also added a cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce a bit.

It's perfect but try it this way as well: marinate the chicken with yoghurt and all the above spices and leave it in fridge overnight! You will remember me. And also if you add chicken bones u add more flavour

WOW!!! This was ABSOLUTLEY DELICIOUS!!!! Tasted restaurant-style. I was blown away by how great this came out. Only thing I changed was that I cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces after browning and I threw in a scotch bonnet for extra heat. Will definitely keep this recipe.

Easy to make and delicious. Have made it about 5 times now with minor tweaks. Every time but the first, I cooked the onions and added the spices, tomatoes and yoghurt, let it simmer to temp and then added chopped chicken with garam masala and cooked it on low for about 30 minutes. I usually add a little extra water, but otherwise stay true to the recipe, adding the cilantro and lemon juice in the last 5 minutes. We reduce the cayenne to 1/4 due to my wife being a wimp, and up the ginger a bit to suit our taste.

This recipe is packed full of flavor. Made as written the first time and it was very good. I now substitute coconut milk in place of the yogurt, add about 2 oz of canned diced green chilis and omit the lemon juice. I also prefer to dice the chicken then cook it. I serve this over yellow jasmine rice and we are lucky if there are any leftovers!

This is by far one of the nicest Indian curry recipies I have ever made! I swapped the the oil for about 30g of butter at the end and cooked it with thighs. I am addicted and have made it so many times. It’s easy and delicious!! The best fake away you could have tastes like A restaurant and so easy!!!

This is really delicious, straightforward and fast to make. I used chicken tenderloins, and substituted 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 1 teaspoon ground cardamom, and 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground pepper for the 1 Tablespoon of curry powder. I only used a dash of cayenne, omitted the 2 teaspoons of salt at the start, and omitted the lemon juice. I served this with rice that had some whole cumin seeds sprinkled on it. Next time I will make more of the sauce!

I love this recipe!!! This curry is a staple iny home and I have cooked it soooo many times for my family. The only differences I make in my recipe are that I dice my chicken, I do not add the extra water, I use coconut milk instead of yogurt, and I add diced green chiles. I also use about half the cayenne pepper called for because I cook for little ones. Tonight I didn't have tumeric and subbed that with smoked paprika and it still came out super delicious!!

I followed as directed. Let the ingredients sit till room temp and had no issue with curdling. I'd like to make it hotter so if there is someone that can share what they did to do that, I'd appreciate it.

Made the recipe with boneless skinless chicken thighs. It was good, but I probably won’t make it again. It did not have the creaminess I thought it would have with the yogurt. In fact the yogurt curdled and separated a little bit.

This recipe looks fantastic! I love how it combines simple ingredients with aromatic spices to create such a rich and comforting curry. It's the perfect dish to enjoy with basmati rice or warm naan. Thanks for sharing such a flavorful recipe—I can't wait to give it a try!
Will definitely make this again. My husband really liked it and so did I.
Just as good as any Curry I've had in a restaurant so far. Now I'm going to play with the spices to try to make it hotter.
It was good and I liked the texture. However, I would add more spices next time as it was not as flavourful as I would have liked.
I love Indian food and this is one of the best recipes I have found for chicken curry. The only thing I did different was double the the spices. I like my curries very spicy.
I have made this my signature dish, we all love it. Thank
Very nice curry how long will it keep in the fridge ? Ps I used double cream instead of yoghurt and it was spot on
